source: Holton, Mackridge & Philippaki-Warburton, Greek: An Essential Grammar, 2nd ed. (Routledge, 2016), upload 418329ba, PDF pp. 45-54 = Ch. 5 (§5.1-5.5). Copyrighted, no open license: rules restated in own words; examples shortened; paradigms and word lists are linguistic facts.

cardinal_ordinal_table.rule: The table gives cardinals and ordinals from 1 to a billion. Several cardinals decline (in the book's table: ένας, τρεις, τέσσερις, the hundreds from 200, χίλιοι and the thousand/million compounds shown with declinable heads); see §5.2. Ordinals all decline like -ος, -η, -ο adjectives (§3.33). Zero is the neuter noun μηδέν (§3.29). When counting, the neuter forms are used: ένα, δύο, τρία, τέσσερα. Punctuation of numerals and decimals: §2.4.
notes: Alternatives are separated by '/'; the first is more common or more neutral, though often a matter of preference.
δύο (two syllables) is more emphatic than δυο (one syllable) and is used in counting; otherwise δυο is the normal form.
Cardinals up to twenty are one word; from twenty-one on, units, tens, hundreds etc. are separate words: τέσσερις χιλιάδες πεντακόσια ενενήντα εννέα 'four thousand five hundred and ninety-nine'.

alphabetic_numerals.rule: A second system uses Greek capital letters (with a following acute-like numeral sign ′) as ordinals, used somewhat like Roman numerals: for chapters or volumes, acts or scenes, centuries, and names of monarchs, popes and patriarchs. Units: Α′=1, Β′=2, Γ′=3, Δ′=4, Ε′=5, ς′=6 (also written ΣΤ′, pronounced στίγμα), Ζ′=7, Η′=8, Θ′=9, Ι′=10. 11-19 combine Ι with the unit (ΙΔ′=14); 20 is Κ′.

examples.el: τον ΙΘ′ αιώνα (= τον δέκατο ένατο αιώνα)
η Βασίλισσα Ελισάβετ Β′ (= η Βασίλισσα Ελισάβετ η δεύτερη)
ο Μιχαήλ Η′ (= ο Μιχαήλ ο όγδοος)

declined_cardinals.rule: ένας, τρεις and τέσσερις, alone or as the last element of a number (except ένδεκα/έντεκα, indeclinable), decline. All numbers ending in 1, 3 or 4 decline alike: δεκατρείς, είκοσι τρεις, τριάντα τρεις; δεκατέσσερις etc.

ένας.note: Almost identical to the indefinite article (§3.7). Fem. μία/μίαν pronounced as two syllables are more emphatic, stressing singularity: μία άποψη 'one point of view' vs μια άποψη 'a point of view'.

μισός_with_numerals.rule: The adjective μισός 'half' combines with cardinals in special forms agreeing with the noun's gender and case. Forms δυόμισι, πεντέμισι, εξήμισι, εφτάμισι, οχτώμισι etc. are indeclinable. Also used for half-hours in telling the time (§5.5, ex. 6).

examples.en: of one and a half hours

hundreds_thousands_millions: Hundreds from διακόσιοι, διακόσιες, διακόσια 'two hundred' follow the plural of -ος adjectives (§3.34); the genitive usually shifts stress to the penultimate syllable: τριακοσίων μέτρων 'of three hundred metres'.
χίλιοι, χίλιες, χίλια 'a thousand' is also an adjective with the same declension and possible genitive stress shift.

From 2,000 the thousands are a cardinal + the feminine plural noun χιλιάδες, with which the numeral agrees (not with the counted noun): είκοσι τρεις χιλιάδες 'twenty-three thousand'; genitive χιλιάδων: δεκατεσσάρων χιλιάδων 'of fourteen thousand'.

εκατομμύριο 'million' and δισεκατομμύριο 'billion' are neuter nouns declined like §3.21: ένα εκατομμύριο; σαράντα τρία εκατομμύρια 'forty-three million'; ένα ποσό των είκοσι ενός εκατομμυρίων ευρώ 'a sum of twenty-one million euros'.

multiplicative.rule: Multiplicative numerals end in -πλός and decline like -ος, -η, -ο adjectives (§3.33).

collective.rule: Collective numerals are feminine nouns with one of two suffixes: -άδα (inclusive, definite number) or -αριά (approximate number; usually preceded by indefinite determiner καμιά).

expressions.title: Numerals in expressions of time, space and quantity

dates.rule: The first of the month: feminine accusative singular of the ordinal. Other days: στις + feminine accusative plural of the cardinal. The month is genitive; the article is normally used with the colloquial month names (ex. 2b). Years: το or στα. For accusative duration/point in time see §3.51.

examples.el: στις είκοσι τέσσερις Σεπτεμβρίου / του Σεπτέμβρη

time_of_day.rule: στη (for one) or στις (other numbers) + feminine accusative of the cardinal; 'o'clock' can be expressed by η ώρα. Minutes with και (past) and παρά (to); half = μισή or the -μισι forms; quarter = τέταρτο.

examples.el: στις πέντε και μισή / στις πεντέμισι

age.rule: Age is expressed with the genitive.

measurement.rule: Height, depth, size and distance use the accusative (§3.51). In expressions of quantity, the measure and the thing measured are in the same case (apposition).

examples.el: ένα κτήριο δεκαπέντε μέτρα ψηλό / ύψος
ένα σίδερο δύο μέτρα μήκος με πέντε εκατοστά φάρδος
examples.en: an iron bar two metres long by five centimetres wide

examples.el: Το χωριό μου είναι έξι χιλιόμετρα μακριά.
examples.en: My village is six kilometres away.
There were two thousand people there.
I bought three kilos of tomatoes.

examples.el: Ο καθένας ήπιε δυο λίτρα νερό.
examples.en: Each person drank two litres of water.
